AI Wardrobe

AI-powered Smart Closet — Auto Cutout, 3D Virtual Try-on, Intelligent Outfit Generator

TRAE AI 创造力大赛 · 生活娱乐赛道 · 2026.07

Requirement Background

The problem

Most people own dozens or even hundreds of clothing items but have no systematic way to manage them. Every morning, you stand in front of a full closet and still feel "I have nothing to wear." When you browse e-commerce platforms and see clothes you like, you save the links but never look back. You want to try new combinations, but pairing items manually is tedious and time-consuming.

Why now

Three technology trends have converged to make this product feasible in 2026:

1. AI background removal has become accessible. Open-source tools like rembg (MIT license) and Meta's SAM/SAM-HQ (Apache 2.0) can isolate clothing from photos with near-professional quality, requiring only a single line of code or a simple API call.[1]

2. Virtual try-on models have reached consumer-grade quality. FASHN VTON v1.5 (Apache 2.0, ~972M parameters) can generate realistic try-on images on a consumer GPU (~8GB VRAM) in about 5 seconds, with no complex mask preprocessing required.[2]

3. Web 3D engines make interactive mannequin display trivial. Three.js provides a lightweight, browser-compatible 3D rendering pipeline that can display parametric human models (SMPL) with drag-to-rotate interaction, no plugins needed.[3]

What happens without it

Users continue to waste time on daily outfit decisions, make impulsive purchases that don't match their existing wardrobe, and let purchased items go unworn. Existing wardrobe apps like Cladwell and Acloset can manage items and suggest combinations, but they only show flat 2D collages—no visual preview of how an outfit actually looks on a person.[4]

Product Vision

AI Wardrobe is a smart closet app that digitizes your entire wardrobe, automatically generates outfit combinations, and previews them on a 3D rotatable mannequin. It bridges the gap between wardrobe management and visual try-on—something no existing consumer product does well.

Core value proposition: Paste a shopping link → AI extracts the clothing flat image → it enters your digital closet → all combinations are generated → each outfit is previewed on a 3D mannequin → swipe to manage your looks.

Functional Requirements

Feature overview

#ModuleFunctional description
F1 Digital Closet Manage all clothing items (tops, bottoms, shoes, accessories). Items can be added via shopping link (AI auto-cut) or photo upload. Each item has a flat image, category tag, color tag, and source link. Users can browse, search, filter, and delete items.
F2 Shopping Link Manager Paste any shopping URL. System fetches the product image, runs AI background removal, and adds the item to the closet. Each link has a status: Purchased / Want to Buy / Watching / Dropped. Users can track purchase intent and manage shopping lists by status.
F3 AI Background Removal Given a product photo (from shopping link or upload), automatically remove the background and produce a clean flat image of the clothing item. The AI detects the clothing region, separates it from the model/mannequin/background, and outputs a transparent-background PNG. Users can manually adjust the crop area if the AI result is unsatisfactory.
F4 Outfit Generator Generate all possible outfit combinations by pairing tops × bottoms × shoes (and optionally accessories). For N items, the system produces up to N¹ × N² × N³ combinations. Each combination is rendered on a 3D mannequin and saved as a look card. Users can set rules to filter (e.g., no shorts in winter, no clash colors).
F5 3D Mannequin Viewer Display a parametric grey human model (based on SMPL) in 3D. The selected outfit's top, bottom, and shoes are texture-mapped onto the model. Users can rotate the model 360 degrees by dragging, zoom in/out. The mannequin supports basic body type adjustment (height range, build range).
F6 Look Swipe Manager Browse generated outfit cards in a Tinder-style swipe interface. Each card shows the outfit on the 3D mannequin. Swipe up = delete (remove from my looks). Swipe left = pending (mark as "maybe"). Swipe right = assign to a look group (e.g., "Work Monday", "Weekend Casual", "Date Night").
F7 Look Groups Organize approved outfits into named groups. Each group represents a scenario or mood (e.g., "Office", "Gym", "Party"). Users can create, rename, reorder, and delete groups. Each group shows a grid of outfit thumbnails. Tapping an outfit opens the 3D mannequin view.

Key module details

F1: Digital Closet

Central repository for all items. Grid view with filter chips (category, color, season). Tap to view item detail and its source link. Batch delete and batch categorize supported.

F2: Shopping Link Manager

Four-tab layout: Purchased / Want to Buy / Watching / Dropped. Paste URL triggers auto-fetch + AI cutout. Tap to view original product page. Drag between tabs to change status.

F4: Outfit Generator

Combination engine pairs items by category. Optionally add rules (color harmony, season filter, style tags). Shows generation progress with count. Results go into the swipe queue.

F6: Look Swipe Manager

Card-based interface. Each card = one outfit on 3D mannequin. Three swipe directions trigger three actions. Visual feedback overlay appears during swipe (delete icon, pending badge, group picker).

↑ Delete | ← Pending | → Assign to Group

LayerTechnologyRationale
Mini-program frontend WeChat Mini-program (native) Primary user-facing platform in China; convenient sharing and daily usage
Web frontend Vue 3 + Three.js Handles 3D mannequin rendering (Three.js) with interactive rotation; Three.js is the most widely adopted Web 3D engine for product display
AI background removal rembg (U2-Net) + SAM-HQ fallback rembg for fast, one-line background removal; SAM-HQ for cases requiring high boundary precision
3D mannequin SMPL parametric model + Three.js renderer SMPL provides industry-standard parametric human body; adjustable body shape and pose; Three.js renders it in browser with drag-to-rotate
Outfit combination Custom engine (Python/Node.js) Cartesian product of category-separated items, with optional rule-based filtering (color harmony, season)
Backend Node.js + SQLite / MongoDB Lightweight for MVP; stores item metadata, outfit records, group assignments
Image storage Cloud OSS (Tencent COS / Alibaba OSS) Clothing images, cutout results, and outfit renderings

AI Quality & Evaluation

Background removal accuracy

MetricTargetMeasurement
Boundary precision (IoU)≥ 0.90Compare AI output mask against manually annotated ground truth on 200 sample images
Category accuracy≥ 0.95Correct classification of item type (top/bottom/shoe/accessory)
User satisfaction≥ 80% accept rateRatio of AI-cut images accepted without manual adjustment
Processing time≤ 3 seconds per imageEnd-to-end from image fetch to cutout result delivery

Fallback mechanisms

If AI background removal produces a low-confidence result (IoU < 0.75 or detected anomaly), the system prompts the user to manually crop instead of auto-adding. For items with complex backgrounds (e.g., model wearing multiple items), the system offers a manual adjustment tool with drag-to-select edges.

Combination explosion management

For a wardrobe with 20 tops, 15 bottoms, and 10 shoes, the total combinations = 20 × 15 × 10 = 3,000 outfits. To prevent overwhelming the user:

  • Batch processing: generate outfits in batches of 50, with a progress indicator
  • Smart sampling: if total combinations exceed 500, randomly sample 500 with diversity constraints (at least one outfit per top, per bottom)
  • Rule-based pruning: user-defined rules (e.g., no white shoes with dark jeans) reduce combinations before rendering

Development Milestones

Phase 1: Foundation (Week 1-2)
Core data model + closet CRUD + manual photo upload

Set up the database schema for items (category, color, image URL, source link, status). Build the mini-program closet grid view. Implement photo upload with basic background removal (rembg). Users can manually add and categorize items.

Phase 2: AI Integration (Week 2-3)
Shopping link parser + auto-cutout + category tagging

Integrate shopping link parsing (support Taobao, JD, Pinduoduo product pages). Auto-fetch product image and run AI cutout. Implement image classification for automatic category and color tagging. Add the four-tab shopping link status manager.

Phase 3: 3D Engine (Week 3-4)
SMPL mannequin + texture mapping + Web 3D viewer

Set up SMPL parametric model in Three.js. Implement texture mapping of clothing flat images onto the mannequin (top/bottom/shoe zones). Build the drag-to-rotate 3D viewer in the Web module. Add basic body type adjustment slider.

Phase 4: Matching & Swipe (Week 4-5)
Combination engine + swipe manager + look groups

Build the exhaustive combination engine with rule-based filtering. Generate outfit cards with 3D mannequin renders. Implement the swipe interface (up=delete, left=pending, right=assign). Build look group management with named collections.

Phase 5: Polish & Submit (Week 5-6)
Performance optimization + UI polish + contest submission

Optimize 3D rendering performance for mobile. Add loading states, empty states, and error handling. Prepare demo video and contest submission materials. Final bug fixing.

Competitive Advantage Summary

Only 3D mannequin in C-end

All existing consumer wardrobe apps show flat collages. AI Wardrobe renders outfits on a rotatable 3D parametric mannequin, giving a real sense of how clothes look on a body.

Shopping link to closet pipeline

No other product offers a seamless flow from e-commerce link to AI cutout to wardrobe entry. This turns browsing into wardrobe building, not just wishlisting.

Exhaustive combination generation

While competitors suggest a handful of outfits, AI Wardrobe generates every possible pairing, ensuring no combination goes undiscovered. Rule-based pruning keeps it manageable.

Gesture-driven look curation

Swipe up/left/right maps to delete/pending/group-assign. This makes reviewing hundreds of outfits fast and intuitive, like a fashion game.
